If the smell lingers too long, dissolve as much washing soda as you can in 10 gallons of cool well water, strain it through a cloth to filter out the excess soda, dump the liquid down the well, then put a hose into the top of the well and let it run for a few hours. A lot of the smell comes from chemicals that are probably more soluble in alkaline water, and the washing soda will make it more alkaline. Then let the hose run on the ground until the washing soda is gone. Then run the hose back into the well for a short time to remove the washing soda from the unsubmerged parts where it might cause corrosion. (If it was my well I'd use lye and plenty of it, but this is tricky to do without expensive damage.)

Decaying plant matter in/around the water table can also make your water stink terribly. That normally happens when something disturbs the area water table (construction involving digging) and causes it to shift, stirring up buried plant matter. The smell may eventually lessen but it'll never go away completely. Cook and drink with bottled water now.
